first_light.reading: more famous than that level predicts
first_light.reading_sentence: Marko Ivanescu is pulling a bigger audience than that level predicts, roughly 2.0 times the predicted figure. First Light expects roughly 0.7M for this level; Marko Ivanescu measures 1.4M.
first_light.note_score: The First Light Index (FLI) compares this fighter's measured audience against what their First Light Rankings level alone would predict, on a -1 to +1 scale. Positive means more famous than that level predicts, negative means that level hasn't been discovered by an audience yet.
first_light.note_audience: Audience is a calibrated followers-equivalent across the platforms we track.
first_light.note_audience_gap: How far this fighter's measured audience sits from what their level alone would predict, in the audience's own units. Positive means more audience than expected, negative means less.

funnel.note: Attention as a ladder: how many people are curious about this fighter, how much of that interest stays between fights, how many people commit by following, and how many of those act on what the fighter posts. Each rung is a different audience, not the same people moving down, and each is set against a typical fighter at the same level.

geography.sentence: Most of Marko Ivanescu's search attention comes from Romania, ahead of United States and Brazil. That market is a small one for advertisers, so the attention there is worth less to a sponsor than the volume alone suggests.
geography.languages_note: The language each reading comes from, the closest free read on audience geography where a country isn't known directly. One language can span many countries (English, Spanish, Portuguese), so this is a rougher cut than the countries above.

compounding.sentence: After each of Marko Ivanescu's last 2 fights, their everyday audience settled higher than before it, about 41% higher on average.
compounding.note: A fight leaving the everyday audience permanently bigger, not just spiking it for a week. Measured well outside the fight's own promotional window and well past its own decay, so a spike never gets mistaken for a durable gain. No rate is projected forward: only what these specific fights showed.

target.sentence: After Marko Ivanescu's last fight, the everyday audience went up 30%. After a fight, rated fighters usually end up +30%. Ivanescu grows the audience about as much as rated fighters usually do after a fight.
target.basis_explainer: Every rated fighter whose audience we measure the same way. Too few fighters sit at this one's level to compare on their own, so the comparison uses the full roster.

differentiators.label: post-fight posting cadence
differentiators.sentence: Among every rated fighter, those who left their everyday audience more durably higher posted on social media about 11 times in the month after the fight; the rest posted 2 times. Ivanescu posted 11 times in the month after their own fight, putting them with the fighters who left their everyday audience more durably higher.
differentiators.note: posts in the month after a fight. Of every rated fighter, 35 did better on durable audience growth after a fight than Ivanescu, 35 did the same or worse.

differentiators.label: short-form video share of posts
differentiators.sentence: Among every rated fighter, those who left their everyday audience more durably higher filled about 44% of their posts with short-form video (Reels and clips); the rest put 10% of their posts in short-form video. Ivanescu filled 33% of their own posts with short-form video, putting them with the fighters who left their everyday audience more durably higher.
differentiators.note: the share of a fighter's posts that are short-form video (Reels/clips) rather than a photo or carousel. Of every rated fighter, 35 did better on durable audience growth after a fight than Ivanescu, 35 did the same or worse.

differentiators.label: per-post engagement rate
differentiators.sentence: Among every rated fighter, those who left their everyday audience more durably higher had about 5.6% of their followers like or comment on each post; the rest had 1.6% of followers engage per post. Ivanescu had 6.1% of their own followers like or comment on each post, putting them with the fighters who left their everyday audience more durably higher.
differentiators.note: the share of a fighter's own followers who like or comment on a typical post. Of every rated fighter, 35 did better on durable audience growth after a fight than Ivanescu, 35 did the same or worse.

differentiators.label: follower growth velocity
differentiators.sentence: Among every rated fighter, those who left their everyday audience more durably higher added about +2.6% more followers than usual in the 30 days after the fight; the rest saw followers move -0.3%. Ivanescu added +2.4% more followers than usual in the 30 days after their own fight, putting them with the fighters who left their everyday audience more durably higher.
differentiators.note: follower growth in the 30 days after a fight, against this fighter's own usual pace. Of every rated fighter, 35 did better on durable audience growth after a fight than Ivanescu, 35 did the same or worse.
